chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Imran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A group of people were brought to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), while he was sitting in the Masjid in Kufa. He found them eating during the day in the month of Ramadan. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to them: 'Did you eat while breaking the fast?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Are you Jews?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'Christians?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'So on what basis are you different from Islam?' They said, 'But we are Muslims.' He said: 'So are you travelers?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'Is there among you an illness that obligates breaking the fast, which we are not aware of, for you are more perceptive of yourselves? Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "But! The human being is evidence against himself."' They said, 'But we have become such that there is no excuse in us.'

He said, so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) smiled, then said: 'Do you testify that there is no god except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' They said, 'We testify that there is no god except Allah, and we do not know Muhammad.' He said: 'But he is the Messenger of Allah.' They said, 'We do not know him with that. Rather, he is a Bedouin who called to himself.' He said: 'If you accept, or else I will surely kill you.' They said, 'Even if you do so.'

So he assigned the Thursday police to them and went out with them to the rear of Kufa. He ordered that two pits be dug, and one was dug beside the other. Then a large hole, like a pomegranate, was pierced between them. He said to them: 'I will place you in one of these two pits and ignite fire in the other, so I will kill you with the smoke.' They said, 'And even if you do so, for rather, this worldly life will end.' So he placed them gently into one of the two pits, then ordered the fire, so it was ignited in the other pit. Then he began calling out to them, time after time: 'What are you saying?' So they answered him: 'Decide what you decide,' until they died.

He said, then he turned away, and the caravans traveled with his deed, and the people discussed it. So one day, while he was in the Masjid, a Jew from the people of Yathrib came to him. The Jews in Yathrib had acknowledged that he was their most knowledgeable, and so had their fathers before him.

He came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) with a number from his family. When they reached the Great Masjid in Kufa, they stabled their mounts, then stood at the door of the Masjid and sent a message to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'We are a group of Jews who have come from Al-Hijaz, and we have a need for you. So will you come out to us, or should we enter to you?'

So he came out to them, and he was saying: 'They will enter and resume with the oath. So what is your need?' So their great one said to him: 'O son of Abu Talib! What is this innovation which you have initiated in the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said to him: 'And which innovation?' So the Jew said to him: 'A group from the people of Al-Hijaz allege that you deliberated to a group who testified that there is no god except Allah and did not acknowledge that Muhammad is His Messenger, so you killed them with the smoke.'

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'So I adjure you by the nine Signs which were revealed to Musa (peace be upon him) at Mount Sinai, and by the right of the five Churches of Jerusalem, and by the right of the Highest Judge; do you know that Joshua ibn Nun was brought a group after the death of Musa, who testified that there is no god except Allah and did not acknowledge that Musa was the Messenger of Allah, so he killed them with a killing similar to this?' So the Jew said to him: 'Yes, I testify that you are the Law of Musa.'

He said, then he brought out a book from his cloak and handed it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he unwrapped it and looked into it and wept. So the Jew said to him: 'What makes you weep, O son of Abu Talib? You merely looked into this book, and it is a Syriac book, and you are an Arab man. So do you know what it is?' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Yes, this is my name, affirmed.' So the Jew said to him: 'So show me your name in this book and inform me what your name is in Syriac.'

He said, so the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) showed him his name in the parchment. He said: 'My name is Eliya.' So the Jew said: 'I testify that there is no god except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and I testify that you are the successor of Muhammad, and I testify that you are the most worthy of the people to the people after Muhammad.' And they pledged allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and entered the Masjid.

So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Praise is to Allah, in Whose Presence I was not forgotten. Praise is to Allah, Who affirmed me in His Presence in the Parchment of the Righteous. And Praise is to Allah, the One with Majesty and Benevolence.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Ali killing people with smoke and the Jew from Yathrib?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *al-Iman al-Mufrad* (isolated faith) by Imam Ali, who executed a group for rejecting Muhammad's prophethood while affirming God's oneness, a unique ruling derived from the Quranic verse 'Man is a witness against himself' (75:2). The narrative further establishes Ali's universal recognition through a Jewish scholar from Yathrib, who verifies the event via a Syriac manuscript bearing Ali's name, thereby confirming his Imamate across religious traditions.
